source_read: Checked against my saved blind-round texts: PMC full texts PMC4091648 (Holmes 2014) and PMC6497989 (Millwood 2019) saved in scratchpad/alc-a/s197/, with my figure readings; the PMC texts of PMC8956974 (Biddinger 2022, with correction PMC9021906) and PMC7299220 (Larsson 2020) as read in my own tab in the blind round, with my figure notes. No page needed reopening; supplements not read.

results.note: All numbers match. 1.15 and 1.12 are slopes per 280 g/week fitted across current-drinker groups whose plotted RRs use the lowest-intake drinkers as reference, not a two-group contrast.

results.corrected_extracted: Coronary heart disease, carriers of the intake-lowering ADH1B variant against non-carriers: odds ratio 0.90 (95% CI 0.84 to 0.96; I² 17%; 46 studies, 20,259 events in 168,731 people); in the four studies with at least 1,000 events (8,374 events), 0.81 (0.72 to 0.91). In the Methods the authors stated that, if the observational U shape were causal, carriers should have higher coronary risk among people drinking more than 0 to under 21 UK units a week and lower risk among people drinking 21 or more.
results.note: Numbers confirmed. 'Before the analysis' cannot be verified: the Methods state the expectation, but no protocol or registration was published; wording changed to 'In the Methods'.

All numbers at the stated places. 'European descent' is in Methods › Formation of the consortium, 2nd paragraph; the carrier definition (dominant model) in Methods › Statistical analysis, 3rd paragraph.
All values match Figure 1, the lifestyle paragraph and Methods › Statistical analysis, 7th paragraph; the contrast with the Discussion is the editors' observation, supported by Figure 1.

results.corrected_extracted: 161,498 adults genotyped for ALDH2 rs671 and ADH1B rs1229984 (151,028 chosen at random). In men, rs671 AA, AG and GG went with mean intakes of 3, 37 and 157 g a week and rs1229984 AA, AG and GG with 98, 106 and 157 g a week; the six genotype–area groups had mean male intakes of 4, 18, 34, 78, 130 and 256 g a week, with 3% to 74% of men ever drinking in most weeks; in women, mean intake was below 2 g a week in groups 1 to 3 and 4 to 8 g a week in groups 4 to 6.
results.corrected_locator: Results, 2nd to 5th paragraphs; Figure 2; Methods › Genotyping and biochemistry, 1st paragraph
results.note: All numbers match; 151,028 (random sample) is in Methods › Genotyping and biochemistry, 1st paragraph, not in Results 2nd–5th; locator extended, text unchanged.
All numbers match. 1.15 and 1.12 are slopes per 280 g/week fitted across current-drinker groups whose plotted RRs use the lowest-intake drinkers as reference, not a two-group contrast.
All values match Table 2 and Results 13th paragraph; 'no copy against one copy' correctly describes GG against AG for the intake-lowering A allele.
All values match Figures 1 and 3 and the text. The text also cites supplement Table X for the smoking-adjusted results, so 'printed only in Figure 3' holds for the main article.

results.corrected_extracted: UK Biobank, 371,463 people of European genetic ancestry; primary score of 5 variants associated with alcohol use disorder, strongly associated with intake (F statistic 780). Linear Mendelian randomization, odds ratio per 1-SD increase in genetically predicted consumption (an SD not defined in the main text): coronary artery disease 1.38 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.74; P = 6.00×10−3); myocardial infarction 1.37 (1.05 to 1.78; P = 2.00×10−2), above the paper's threshold of P < .008 for six diseases. Weighted median, MR-Egger, MR-PRESSO and analyses excluding abstainers pointed the same way.
results.corrected_locator: Methods › Study Population; Methods › Genetic Instruments for Alcohol Consumption; Results › Associations Between Genetic Instruments and Alcohol Intake Phenotypes; Results › Traditional MR, 2nd paragraph; Table 2
results.note: Values match; 371,463 (European ancestry) and the 5-variant score are only in Methods (Study Population; Genetic Instruments); locator extended. Secondary-method agreement is the authors' statement; values only in supplement.

results.corrected_extracted: Nonlinear Mendelian randomization with the primary score: quadratic models fitted best for coronary artery disease and hypertension (P < .001), with every amount of intake associated with higher risk, rising more steeply at higher intake; the fitted curves print no values. With the secondary score (10 variants for the AUDIT-C consumption score), piecewise analyses suggested no rise in cardiovascular risk until roughly 7 to 14 drinks a week, with slight decreases at modest intake for hypertension and in some analyses in women, which the authors attribute to pleiotropy in that score and low power.
results.corrected_locator: Methods › Genetic Instruments for Alcohol Consumption; Results › Evaluating Association Shapes, 1st to 3rd paragraphs; Figures 2 and 3
results.note: 10-variant count is in Methods; locator extended, text unchanged. The main text does not name the score used for the piecewise threshold (eFigure 9, unread); AUDIT-C-R follows from the sentence but is not explicit.

results.corrected_extracted: In 34,423 lifelong abstainers the score showed no association with the continuous traits reported in that paragraph (the main text gives no disease results for abstainers), except HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein A, which the authors call a potential pleiotropic effect; MR-Egger intercepts were non-significant. The authors acknowledge that the associations may reflect genes that influence both drinking and cardiovascular disease rather than an effect of alcohol, and that variants for diagnosed alcohol use disorder are an indirect proxy for usual intake.
results.note: The main text's abstainer check concerns continuous traits (GGT, blood pressure, LDL; HDL and apolipoprotein A flagged). No disease results for abstainers are printed, so 'the outcomes' overstates it. Limitations confirmed.

All numbers at the stated places. 'European descent' is in Methods › Formation of the consortium, 2nd paragraph; the carrier definition (dominant model) in Methods › Statistical analysis, 3rd paragraph.

results.corrected_extracted: 512,715 adults from ten areas of China, enrolled 2004–2008 and followed about 10 years to 1 January 2017 (0.9% lost to follow-up); 161,498 genotyped for ALDH2 rs671 and ADH1B rs1229984. The six genotype–area groups had mean male intakes of 4, 18, 34, 78, 130 and 256 g a week, with 3%, 15%, 20%, 39%, 60% and 74% of men ever drinking in most weeks; in women, mean intake was below 2 g a week in groups 1 to 3 and 4 to 8 g a week in groups 4 to 6.
results.corrected_locator: Methods › Study design and participants, 1st paragraph; Results, 1st, 2nd and 5th paragraphs; Figure 2
results.note: All numbers match; 161,498 genotyped is in Results 2nd paragraph (and Methods › Genotyping and biochemistry), not in the 1st or 5th; locator extended, text unchanged.
All values match Table 2 and Results 12th–13th paragraphs (P 0.0007 and <0.0001; in women no significant single-variant associations with stroke).

results.corrected_extracted: Per SD of genetically predicted log drinks a week (up to 94 variants; European descent): stroke (76,814 cases) odds ratio 1.27 (95% CI 1.12 to 1.45; P = 2.87×10−4), 1.21 (1.05 to 1.40; P = 0.010) after adjustment for genetic liability to smoking initiation; ischaemic stroke 1.26 (1.09 to 1.46; P = 0.002; 64,943 cases) and intracerebral haemorrhage 3.53 (1.70 to 7.32; P = 0.001; 2,609 cases), combining consortium and UK Biobank data; subarachnoid haemorrhage in UK Biobank 2.47 (1.08 to 5.62).
results.corrected_locator: Abstract (Methods); Figure 1; Results › Associations With CVD, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Figures 3 and 4
results.note: Values match; 'up to 94 variants' is in the Abstract (Methods); locator extended. 'European descent' fits the instrument; MEGASTROKE outcome data were not restricted to it (similar when restricted).
Values match Tables 1 and 2. 8,710 is the whole-sample count (Table 1); the number of strokes in the MR analysis (current drinkers, Table 2 footnote) is not printed.

results.corrected_extracted: Men: systolic blood pressure rose 4.8 mm Hg (95% CI 4.5 to 5.1) per 280 g a week of usual self-reported intake among current drinkers (conventional analysis of 193,003 men in all drinking categories, Figure 3A) and 4.3 mm Hg (3.7 to 4.9) per 280 g a week of genotype-predicted mean intake (55,897 men in Figure 3, 55,879 in Table 2); HDL cholesterol rose 0.19 and 0.16 mmol/L and γ-glutamyltransferase 62 and 44 IU/L in the conventional and genetic analyses respectively.
results.note: 193,003 is all men in the conventional panel across drinking categories (Figure 3A), not current drinkers (69,897 men drank in most weeks). Other values match Figure 3, Table 2 and Results 6th paragraph.
All values match Table 2 (women n 83,017 for blood pressure; P <0.0001 for a larger effect in men) and Results 12th paragraph.
All values match Table 2 and the biomarkers paragraph (waist −0.34 cm in Table 2; the abstract rounds it to −0.3).
Values match Tables 1 and 2 and Traditional MR, 1st paragraph. 121,708 is the whole-sample count; cases in the MR analysis (current drinkers) are not printed.
All counts match Figure 1; Figure 3 gives venous thromboembolism non-cases as 353,589 against 353,489 here (a discrepancy within the source).
All values match Figure 3 and the text (random-effects IVW). Smoking-adjusted values are also cited to supplement Table X; within the main article they are printed only in Figure 3.
Matches Strengths and Limitations, 3rd paragraph (the source says the UK Biobank overlap applies to most analyses) and the smoking-initiation OR in the Results.
Values match Tables 1 and 2 and the text; 14,367 and 5,812 are whole-sample counts (Table 1), not the cases analysed in current drinkers.
